scope: Real disk reads of prepared per-method container files (one whole, one chunk_size=256 chunked, per codec method) followed by horizon.town_disk decode, on this machine only. "full" times reconstructing the entire map from each container; "partial" times retrieving one exact, grid-aligned chunk via a true single-chunk read against decoding the whole container and cropping an owned copy out of it. Chunk-index/header overhead is included in the chunked timings and byte counts as read off disk -- it is not subtracted out. There is no multi-chunk arbitrary-ROI engine here: region() only ever addresses one exact chunk on the fixed chunk_size=256 grid, never an arbitrary rectangle spanning chunk boundaries. warm_buffered is explicitly primed by this script (see priming_policy). macos_nocache only requests fcntl(F_NOCACHE) on the reading handle (see priming_policy for what that does and does not establish); it is not a verified physically cold read. bytes_read/bytes_requested/read_calls are the application-level read() syscall counts horizon.town_disk's reader itself tallies, not a measurement of physical SSD/controller transfer size.

settings.order_policy: per repeat, swap execution order of the measured pair (whole vs. chunked) by repeat index parity: even repeats run whole-first, odd repeats run chunk-first; applied independently to the full workload and the partial workload. Mode and method ordering is static (outer loops: method, then mode), not alternated -- recorded here as a caveat rather than implemented, since both are set once per run from --modes/METHODS and the per-repeat whole/chunk swap already covers the dominant ordering bias within a (method, mode) cell.
settings.region_schedule_policy: per repeat, a pixel coordinate (row_px, col_px) is drawn uniformly at random from the seeded RNG via Generator.integers(0, size) independently per axis -- every pixel in [0, size-1], including the last row/column, is reachable with equal probability. That pixel is mapped to its exact, grid-aligned chunk_size=256 chunk (edge chunks shrink to fit, same convention as horizon.chunk_benchmark). One schedule entry is drawn per repeat (length == --repeats, no truncation), and the same per-repeat schedule of pixels/chunks is reused for every method and mode. Both the drawn pixel and the resulting region are recorded per repeat.
settings.priming_policy: warm_buffered: before every measured load_whole/load_chunked call, this script does one untimed ordinary buffered read of BOTH the whole container file and the chunked container file for that method, regardless of which one is about to be measured, so both files are symmetrically warmed in the OS page cache. macos_nocache: no priming is performed by this script; this is NOT a claim of a physically cold read. horizon.town_disk only requests fcntl(fd, F_NOCACHE, 1) on the reading descriptor -- it has not been verified to evict any page, and it has not been verified to reach the SSD/controller/drive cache. It is also not a claim that the OS page cache never serves this read from pages already resident from an earlier warmup, repeat, or process: F_NOCACHE is only documented to stop this descriptor from retaining newly read data in the cache, not to force every read to bypass already-cached pages.
